Chartography: A Benchmark for Professional Chart Understanding

paper.arxiv.2608.10677

Prepared 15 Nov 2026 · Evidence snapshot 12 Nov 2026 · Report research-2026-11-12.1 · Evidence research-2026-11-11.candidate.1

Evidence & scope

Substantive bounded primary methods/results/limitations source review is documented at 2608.10677v1. Independent expert task review and repeated-trial/self-judge metric conditions establish benchmark creation.100tasks and98images remain distinct units; no corpus or CI calibration audit implied. Original author/source-verifier/adversarial receipts bind every exact approved fact; unread pages, unreplicated experiments and source conflicts remain recorded in the pinned dossier. This admission is for one logical paper work only.

Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Items are adversarially screened and require specialist standing knowledge under a no-tools single-image protocol. The judge shares identity with an evaluated configuration, and online chart provenance does not establish redistribution rights. Results do not estimate general professional decision accuracy, deployed agent performance or causal superiority of a specific visual mechanism.

Permanent record ID: repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.mandatory3.claim.arxiv.2608.10677.limitation

  • This is a source-specific, first-party description; this repair does not independently reproduce experiments or audit operational execution and customer outcomes.
  • The benchmark has 100 selected tasks, twelve domain labels and 98 byte-distinct images. Professionals select/create charts, write objective questions, walkthroughs and ranges; three additional experts verify each task and at least one frontier failure is required for retention.
  • Twenty no-tools trials per task yield 2,000 scored responses per configuration, not 2,000 independently sampled tasks. Gemini 3.5 Flash grades equivalence to expert answers/ranges without seeing the chart; multipart answers are all-or-nothing and its own leaderboard entry is self-judging.
  • Table 3 freezes the July 2026 snapshot, reporting mean pass@1 and 95% confidence intervals. Display ranks and overlapping intervals do not establish statistically distinct capability tiers.
  • Eighty-one charts are online-sourced and nineteen are author-created. Provenance is reported; this repair does not independently establish redistribution rights for each image.
  • Failure explanations derive from qualitative trajectory review. This author did not audit judge validity, CI coverage or task corpus, and does not interpret the explanations as a controlled perception-versus-reasoning causal ablation.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Chartography uses 100 professionally authored chart questions verified by three additional experts and screened for at least one meaningful frontier-model failure. Each configuration receives 20 no-tools trials per task; Gemini 3.5 Flash judges the final answer against expert targets/ranges without seeing the chart, and multipart answers require all parts.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

The frozen July 2026 table reports 45.0% mean pass@1 for the leading configuration across 100 tasks × 20 scored trials, with a reported 95% CI half-width 1.1 percentage points. The metric is the fraction of all graded trials passed; displayed ranks and overlapping intervals should not be interpreted as statistically distinct capability tiers.
